gloss: sacred tree (at a shrine or temple)

definitions.gloss: sacred tree at a shrine or temple
definitions.explanation: A tree on the grounds of a Shinto shrine (or sometimes a Buddhist temple) that is regarded as sacred, often believed to house or attract a divine spirit. Typically marked off with a {注連縄|しめなわ} (sacred rope) tied around the trunk.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}の{御神木|ごしんぼく}に{手|て}を{合|あ}わせた。
examples.english: I put my hands together in prayer at the shrine's sacred tree.

examples.japanese: この{御神木|ごしんぼく}は{樹齢|じゅれい}{千|せん}{年|ねん}を{超|こ}えると{伝|つた}えられている。
examples.english: This sacred tree is said to be over a thousand years old.

examples.japanese: {御神木|ごしんぼく}の{周|まわ}りには{注連縄|しめなわ}が{張|は}られていた。
examples.english: A sacred rope had been hung around the sacred tree.

notes:
Compound of the honorific {御|ご} + {神|しん} (god, deity) + {木|ぼく} (tree). Often a large, ancient {老木|ろうぼく} (old tree) believed to embody or attract a {神|かみ}. Cutting or damaging one is treated as a serious taboo.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神社|じんじゃ}の{御神木|ごしんぼく}: sacred tree of the shrine
- {御神木|ごしんぼく}に{手|て}を{合|あ}わせる: to pray at a sacred tree
- {御神木|ごしんぼく}{信仰|しんこう}: belief in sacred trees

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Shinto, certain natural features—trees, rocks, mountains—are considered to be {依|よ}り{代|しろ}, places where a deity can descend or reside. A {御神木|ごしんぼく} is one of the most common manifestations of this belief; it is marked with a {注連縄|しめなわ} and treated with reverence.
